source_summary: Tall ink-and-wash Chinese landscape with steep rocky mountains, mist-filled valleys, layered watercourses, pine groves, small pavilion/bridge structures, lower hamlet, and foreground stream banks; calligraphy, seals, borders, and paper texture are excluded.

motifs.name: upper_left_cliff_peak
motifs.description: Isolate the large upper-left rocky mountain mass with its sheer cliff faces, rounded boulders, narrow ledges, pine clusters on the summit and slopes, and the small angular roof or lookout structure near the top edge of the cliff.
must_preserve: dry ink contour lines defining fractured rock planes
layered gray-brown wash on cliff faces
dark pine needle clusters along the crest and left slope
small roof geometry tucked against the summit ledge
fine vertical texture strokes and dotted moss marks

motifs.name: central_misty_peaks
motifs.description: Isolate the distant vertical mountain silhouettes rising in the central background beyond the valley, including soft-edged peaks partially submerged in mist.
must_preserve: soft diluted wash gradients
blurred mist edges around the peak bases
tall narrow peak silhouettes
faint tonal separation between nearer and farther forms

motifs.name: right_mid_cliff_grove
motifs.description: Isolate the right-side midground cliff with the pine-covered top, steep rock wall, and small lower spur descending toward the water.
must_preserve: dark clustered pine crowns at the upper right
angular cliff outlines and ledge contours
vertical rock texture strokes
small scrub dots along the slope
washed shadow separating cliff from misty background

motifs.name: middle_water_pavilion_bridge
motifs.description: Isolate the mid-level water terrace with rippling stream patterns, the horizontal bridge or walkway, and the compact pavilion/roof cluster embedded among straight pines.
motifs.role: pavilion group with bridge over water
must_preserve: thin parallel roof and bridge lines
dark vertical pine trunks framing the structures
tiny tiled roof angles
flowing water-line curls around the banks
ink contrast between architecture and pale water wash

motifs.name: central_gorge_cascade
motifs.description: Isolate the central descending gorge where pale water drops through a narrow ravine between cliffs, with flanking pines, bare branches, stone ledges, and stepped banks.
must_preserve: light unpainted cascade channel
stepped contour lines along the ravine walls
dark pine silhouettes on both sides
bare twig-like branches crossing the rocks
moss dots and broken texture strokes on the cliff faces

motifs.name: lower_left_hamlet_path
motifs.description: Isolate the lower-left sheltered hamlet area with small roofed buildings, dark tree canopy, winding stair path, rock walls, and dense surrounding shrubs.
must_preserve: small hut roof geometry and dark eaves
curving stepped path lines
dense black ink foliage masses
rock contours enclosing the settlement
fine shrub and bamboo-like strokes around the buildings

motifs.name: central_foreground_tree_grove
motifs.description: Isolate the central foreground grove on the rocky slope, including tall straight pines, a bare-branched tree, bamboo-like foliage, shrubs, and mottled rock texture beneath.
must_preserve: vertical pine trunks with dark needle clusters
bare angular branch network
bamboo-like leaf strokes near the lower center
granular moss-dot texture on the rocks
layered ink washes shaping the slope

motifs.name: foreground_stream_willows_rocks
motifs.description: Isolate the bottom foreground stream bank with willow trees, rounded shrubs, scattered stones, rippling water lines, and low rocky embankments, excluding any seal marks at the lower edge.
must_preserve: long drooping willow branch lines
rounded pebble and stone clusters
thin horizontal water ripples
dark stippled shoreline vegetation
low rock contours and pale water-wash transitions

planning_prompt:
Analyze this Chinese landscape painting as a source for a motif bank.

Create exactly 8 reusable motifs. Return JSON only.

For each motif:
- Use a short snake_case name.
- Describe what should be isolated.
- Provide a normalized bbox as [x, y, width, height], where 0,0 is the top-left of the full image.
- Include all visible brushwork for that motif, but do not include unrelated neighboring motifs.
- Prefer motifs that can be recombined into a new coherent Chinese painting: mountains, hillsides, village clusters, pavilion groups, water/lotus surfaces, bridges, scholar figures, boats, clouds, rocks, shrubs, pines, willows, bamboo.
- Capture details that must be preserved: linework, wash texture, roof geometry, tree needles, rock texture, mist edges, and color accents.

Do not invent objects that are not visible in the source image.
Do not include calligraphy, seals, labels, borders, or paper texture as motifs unless explicitly requested.
